title: Report intentional damage or graffiti to NSW Police
summary: You can report intentional damage or graffiti to your property online through the NSW Police.
intro: If your property has been intentionally damaged, destroyed or graffitied, you can complete a police report online.
who_can_apply: The damage must be intentional, not normal wear and tear or an accident.
The damage must not be caused by a traffic crash, fire, or attempt to gain entry to a premises (in which case, call 131 444).
If the incident is an emergency or happening now, call Triple Zero (000).
what_you_need: A description of the damaged property, including the location, the owner's contact details, the estimated value of the damage, and the date and time of the incident (if known).
Photos of the damaged property (if available).

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to submit your online police report.
you can track it and receive electronic status updates
you’ll receive a NSW Police Force Event number for insurance purposes (if applicable).

more_info.text: Police reports may be referred to as online malicious damage reports, or online damaged property reports.

internal_links.text: Report graffiti on community facilities or public assets
Access the NSW Police Force Community Portal

faqs.q: What types of damage can I report online?
faqs.a: You can report intentional damage or graffiti online, but normal wear and tear or accidents are not considered intentional damage.

faqs.q: What should I do if the damage is an emergency?
faqs.a: If the incident is an emergency or happening now, call Triple Zero (000) immediately.

faqs.q: How do I report damage caused by a traffic crash or fire?
faqs.a: If the damage is caused by a traffic crash or fire, or an attempt to gain entry to a premises, call the Police Assistance Line on 131 444.
